Assign reference items to splits by cluster

Source: R/core-harness-splits.R
hr_assign_splits.Rd

Puts every item of a cluster (a document, usually) in the same split, so that no document has items on both sides of a tuning and a scoring split. The assignment is worked out from the seed and the cluster ids alone: the order of the rows, the session's random state and the other clusters in the set do not change it (with method = "stable").

Usage

hr_assign_splits(
  items,
  cluster = NULL,
  props = c(dev = 0.1, exploratory = 0.1, calibration = 0.3, test = 0.5),
  seed,
  method = c("stable", "balanced")
)

Arguments

items

The items: a vector of item ids, or a data frame with one row per item. A data frame's ids come from its item_id column, else its id column, else the row number. Column names are matched exactly, so a column such as ideal_answer is never taken for id.

cluster

The cluster of each item: a vector as long as items, or for a data frame the name of a column. With a data frame one string is always read as a column name; for a one-row frame and a literal cluster value, wrap it in I(). NULL takes a data frame's cluster column, else its document column; for a vector of ids, or a data frame with neither column, each item is its own cluster.

props

Named shares, from "dev", "exploratory", "calibration", "test" and "final", each at least 0, adding up to 1.

seed

One number or one string. Required: the assignment is a function of the seed and the ids, so the seed has to be recorded with it.

method

"stable" or "balanced"; see "How clusters are assigned".

Value

An object of class hr_splits, a list with:

items

The items with a split column: the data frame given, or a data frame of item_id, cluster and split.

clusters

One row per cluster: cluster, n_items, u and split.

counts

One row per split in props: split, target (the share asked for), clusters, items, cluster_share and item_share.

props, seed, method

As given.

notes

Remarks, such as a split that was given a share and received no cluster.

It has a print() method.

The splits

  • dev tunes prompts, settings and margins. Its scores are not evidence.

  • exploratory is kept out of the test set for exploratory comparisons.

  • calibration is for calibrating signals and choosing gate thresholds (hr_calibrate_signal(), hr_gate_threshold()), kept apart from both tuning and testing.

  • test is what reported comparisons are scored on.

  • final is an optional held-back set, run once per release.

props names any of these. A split given a share of 0 receives nothing.

How clusters are assigned

Each cluster gets a number u in [0, 1) from the first 13 hex digits of the SHA-256 digest of "harnessr-split", the seed and the cluster id (as UTF-8, joined by a separator), divided by 16^13. A number that is a whole number is written out in full before it is hashed, so a document id of 100000 gets the same split whether it is stored as a double or as an integer (as.character(100000) would give "1e+05").

  • method = "stable" (the default) cuts [0, 1) into consecutive intervals whose widths are props, in the order props is given, and a cluster goes to the interval u falls in. A cluster's split depends only on the seed and its own id, so adding documents to the set later, or dropping some, never moves another document between splits. The shares are those of props on average over clusters; with few clusters they can be some way off, and counts shows how far.

  • method = "balanced" sorts the clusters by u and gives each split its share of the clusters, rounded by largest remainders (Hamilton's method), in the order props is given. The number of clusters per split is then as close to props as whole clusters allow, but a cluster added later can shift others across a boundary, so the assignment should be drawn once and stored.

Shares are shares of clusters. Item counts follow from cluster sizes and are reported beside them.

See also

gr_label_sheet() to write sheets for people to label the items, hr_calibrate_signal().

Other reference sets: gr_label_sheet(), gr_read_labels()

Examples

qa <- data.frame(item_id = sprintf("q%02d", 1:40),
                 document = rep(sprintf("doc%02d.pdf", 1:10), each = 4))
sp <- hr_assign_splits(qa, seed = 2026)
sp
#> <hr_splits> 40 item(s) in 10 cluster(s), method stable, seed 2026
#> 
#>        split target clusters items cluster_share item_share
#>          dev    0.1        1     4           0.1        0.1
#>  exploratory    0.1        2     8           0.2        0.2
#>  calibration    0.3        1     4           0.1        0.1
#>         test    0.5        6    24           0.6        0.6
table(sp$items$split)
#> 
#> calibration         dev exploratory        test 
#>           4           4           8          24 

# Whole clusters, split as close to the shares as ten documents allow.
hr_assign_splits(qa, seed = 2026, method = "balanced")$counts
#>         split target clusters items cluster_share item_share
#> 1         dev    0.1        1     4           0.1        0.1
#> 2 exploratory    0.1        1     4           0.1        0.1
#> 3 calibration    0.3        3    12           0.3        0.3
#> 4        test    0.5        5    20           0.5        0.5
